# Scrapfly Scrapers

> Example web scrapers for 81 popular websites (Amazon, eBay, Zillow, Booking.com and more), written in Python with the Scrapfly SDK, one folder per website. Each scraper is a short module of async functions that return JSON-ready data, with an example script (`run.py`), live tests (`test.py`) and sample output (`results/`).

These scrapers are educational examples that accompany the Scrapfly scrape guides: copy one and adapt it, they are not an installable library. Every request goes through the Scrapfly API, so a Scrapfly API key is needed (https://scrapfly.io/register, then https://scrapfly.io/dashboard).

## When an agent should use this repository

- The user wants data from one of the websites listed under "Scrapers": start from that folder instead of writing a scraper from scratch.
- The user wants to scrape a similar website: copy the scraper of the closest website (same kind of pages: search results, product, property, profile, reviews) and adapt its URLs, parsing and tests.
- The user wants to learn how a website is scraped: most folders link a step-by-step guide.

## Use a scraper

```bash
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/amazon-scraper        # any <name>-scraper folder
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="your API key"         # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root                   # Python 3.10+
poetry run python run.py                   # example scrape, writes results/*.json
poetry run pytest test.py -k test_search   # live tests, one test at a time with -k
```

From Python, inside the scraper folder:

```python
import asyncio
import amazon  # the module has the name of the folder without "-scraper"

results = asyncio.run(amazon.scrape_search("https://www.amazon.com/s?k=kindle", max_pages=1))
```

- The module reads `SCRAPFLY_KEY` from the environment when it is imported.
- In most modules `BASE_CONFIG` holds the Scrapfly settings sent with every request (anti-bot bypass, country, ...); change an entry there (for example `BASE_CONFIG["cache"] = True`) rather than every request.
- The functions return plain dicts and lists; `results/` holds the output `run.py` produced with them.
- `run.py` and the tests scrape the live websites, so they use Scrapfly credits and fail when a website changes.

## Scrapers

Each entry: the folder, its scrape guide, its sample output and its public functions (`async`, run them with `asyncio.run` or `await`).

- **Air France** (`airfrance-scraper/`): [code](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/tree/main/airfrance-scraper) | guide: [How to Scrape Air France Flights with Python (2026)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-air-france-flights) | sample output: [Roundtrip](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/airfrance-scraper/results/roundtrip.json)
  - `scrape_flights(origin, destination, departure_date, return_date, max_retries=3)`: (not async) Scrape flight offers from Air France search GraphQL XHR.
- **Airbnb.com** (`airbnb-scraper/`): [code](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/tree/main/airbnb-scraper) | guide: [How to Scrape Airbnb Listings and Prices (2026)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-airbnb) | sample output: [Property](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/airbnb-scraper/results/property.json), [Search](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/airbnb-scraper/results/search.json)
  - `scrape_listings(query, check_in=None, check_out=None, adults=1, max_pages=3)`: scrape Airbnb search results for a location
  - `scrape_properties(urls, check_in=None, check_out=None, adults=1)`: scrape Airbnb property pages
- **Aliexpress.com** (`aliexpress-scraper/`): [code](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/tree/main/aliexpress-scraper) | guide: [How to Scrape Aliexpress.com (2025 Update)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-aliexpress) | sample output: [Product pages](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/aliexpress-scraper/results/product.json), [Search pages](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/aliexpress-scraper/results/search.json), [Product reviews](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/aliexpress-scraper/results/reviews.json), [Category products](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/aliexpress-scraper/results/category_products.json)
  - `scrape_search(url, max_pages=60)`: Scrape all search results and return parsed search result data
  - `scrape_product(url)`: scrape aliexpress products by id
  - `scrape_product_reviews(product_id, max_scrape_pages=None)`: scrape all reviews of aliexpress product
- **Allegro.pl** (`allegro-scraper/`): [code](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/tree/main/allegro-scraper) | guide: [How to Scrape Allegro.pl in 2026 (Without Getting Blocked)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-allegro) | sample output: [Product](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/allegro-scraper/results/product.json), [Search](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/allegro-scraper/results/search.json)
  - `scrape_search(query, max_pages=3, scrape_all_pages=False)`: Scrape Allegro search pages for product listings
  - `scrape_product(urls)`: scrape a single Allegro product
- **Amazon.com** (`amazon-scraper/`): [code](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/tree/main/amazon-scraper) | guide: [How to Scrape Amazon.com Product Data and Reviews](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-amazon) | sample output: [Product pages](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/amazon-scraper/results/product.json), [Search pages](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/amazon-scraper/results/search.json), [Product reviews](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/amazon-scraper/results/reviews.json)
  - `scrape_search(url, max_pages=None)`: Scrape amazon search pages product previews
  - `scrape_reviews(url)`: scrape product reviews of a given URL of an amazon product
  - `scrape_product(url)`: scrape Amazon.com product
- **App Store** (`app-store-scraper/`): [code](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/tree/main/app-store-scraper) | sample output: [App metadata](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/app-store-scraper/results/app_metadata.json), [Reviews](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/main/app-store-scraper/results/reviews.json)
  - `scrape_app_metadata(app_id, country='us')`: scrape app metadata via the iTunes lookup API, falling back to the apps.apple.com page
  - `scrape_reviews(app_id, country='us', max_pages=None)`: scrape app reviews via the iTunes customer reviews RSS feed

  - `scrape_reviews(skuid, max_pages=None)`: scrape review data from the reviews API

## Write a new scraper

Follow the layout and style of the existing folders (the maintainers' rules):

1. Create a `<name>-scraper/` folder with:
   - `<name>.py`: all the scraper code;
   - `run.py`: runs the scraper on example URLs and saves the output to `results/*.json`;
   - `test.py`: pytest tests that check live output against a [cerberus](https://docs.python-cerberus.org/) schema;
   - `results/`: the sample output written by `run.py`;
   - `README.md`: a copy of another scraper's README with the website name changed;
   - `pyproject.toml`: a Poetry project like the other folders (no `poetry.lock`, so users get the latest SDK).
2. Code:
   - top-level `async def scrape_*()` functions such as `scrape_search(url, max_pages=...)` and `scrape_products(urls)`, with small synchronous `parse_*()` helpers;
   - one module-level `SCRAPFLY = ScrapflyClient(key=os.environ["SCRAPFLY_KEY"])` and a `BASE_CONFIG` dict spread into every `ScrapeConfig(url, **BASE_CONFIG)`;
   - several URLs at once with `SCRAPFLY.concurrent_scrape()`, with the concurrency limit set to automatic;
   - prefer the JSON data hidden in the page over HTML selectors, keep results flat, use type hints and short comments, keep it simple: the code is for learning;
   - inputs are full URLs rather than values the scraper turns into URLs; use small defaults (pages, items).
3. Tests: one schema per result type plus length checks (for example a search returns at least N items); mark them with `@pytest.mark.asyncio` and `@pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=3, reruns_delay=30)`, with `pytest-rerunfailures` in the dev dependencies.
4. Nothing to add to the CI: the nightly run tests every `test_*` function of every `test.py` (tests that must not run are listed in `.github/test_matrix_exclude.txt`).
5. Run `python .github/scripts/docs.py` to add the scraper to the README table and to this file; put its website name, guide and sample dataset labels in `.github/scrapers.json` when the defaults are not right.

To start, copy the folder of a listed scraper for a similar website and keep its structure.
